$comment: THE ONE SOURCE. Product brief section 2.6: the palette, type scale,
spacing scale and radii live in one file and are exported to CSS custom
properties and to Dart constants by a build step. Neither client
hardcodes a colour.
That is not tidiness. Two clients shipping in parallel drift the moment a
hex value exists in two places, and section 0 makes it explicit: a
colour, spacing value or label that differs between web and native is a
bug. Acceptance criterion 10 is that a change here updates both.
Regenerate with:  python tools/tokens.py
Checked by:       tests/test_tokens.py, which fails if either export is
stale - so a token changed here and not exported is a
test failure rather than a visual surprise later.

core.$comment: Product brief 6.1. Six values, and no seventh without a reason written here.

etch.use: rules, borders, grid lines, inactive strokes

phosphor.use: primary accent, active state, primary actions, focused input
phosphor.why: The amber phosphor value, chosen over the obvious terminal green so the product does not read as a generic hacker skin. Green appears only as a state colour.

grid.use: the graticule ruled over the app ground
grid.why: The SEVENTH core value, and the note this file demands for one. It is `case` lightened, it is already named in bpcad_media/README.md, and the design handoff draws a graticule on every ground - so it was going to be written somewhere. Written here it stays equal on both clients; written in two stylesheets it does not.

$comment: Product brief 6.1. USED ONLY INSIDE THE 3D CANVAS AND FOR ANNOTATION.
A plotter pen set, where different line types mean different things -
which is why these are separate from the core palette and must not be
borrowed for chrome.
Every pen is paired with an icon or a label in the UI: brief 6.7
forbids colour-only status signalling.

ref.meaning: reference body from a photo, never printed

pass.meaning: passed check, confirmed dimension, joint clearance OK

warn.meaning: tolerance risk, uncalibrated default, thin wall

fail.meaning: failed check, interpenetration, out of bed bounds
fail.why: Magenta rather than red, because it comes from the plotter pen set and because red is reserved for destructive confirmation only.

$comment: Product brief 6.2. Two families, clearly distinct, and monospace is
functional rather than decorative: parameter digits must not shift
width while a slider moves. Every numeric field sets tabular-nums.
Prose is a neutral grotesque because monospace paragraphs are hostile
to read - onboarding, errors and help are prose, not data.

mono.stack: 'IBM Plex Mono', 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'DejaVu Sans Mono', monospace
mono.use: labels, parameters, numbers, dimensions, the command line, the coordinate readout, buttons

scale.$comment: px. Sentence case throughout; no tracked-out all-caps labels.

space.$comment: px. A 4-based scale; every gap in either client is one of these.

$comment: px. Squared-off rather than pill-shaped: this is a machine, not a toy.
TWO STEPS ADDED FOR THE GLASS LAYER (design handoff, TOKENS.md). The
scale topped out at 10 and a floating sheet needs more, so `control`
and `float` were added rather than hardcoded at the call site.
The split matters more than the numbers: soft radii belong to floating
SURFACES, and 0/3 stay on DATA marks - check marks, status squares,
slider thumbs, progress bars, dot indicators. That contrast is what
stops the glass reading as a generic consumer app, and it is the one
thing to preserve if these values are ever retuned.
THE GLASS LAYER. Design handoff README section 6, accepted as an
amendment to product brief 6.6.
Every raised surface is glass. What stays flat is the app ground and
its graticule, the 3D canvas, and INK - text, numbers, dimension
callouts, sliders and check marks are full opacity and never
translucent. Glass is the surface under a value, never the value.
The rule that keeps it legible: a surface over CONTENT is denser than
one over the GROUND. That is what the five steps below are - not five
shades of grey, five depths. Do not go below a step's alpha.
The tint is exported as a triplet rather than as five colours so a
theme change moves all of it: CSS composes rgb(var(--bp-glass-tint) /
alpha), Dart calls BpGlass.tint(alpha).

tint.use: the fill every glass surface is built from, at the alpha of its step

highlight.use: inset top highlight, the light catching the top edge of the pane

surface.$comment: The five depths, shallowest first. `blur` is px.

panel.use: sits over the ground: web side columns, scrollback, the photo-fit invitation

well.use: recessed in a panel: field wells, segmented controls, rail items

card.use: library cards, plan cards, notes, the credits panel, the avatar

pill.use: over the viewport: the composer, viewport pills, browser chrome

float.use: over everything: the bottom sheet, the device bezel, the tab bar, the web status line

$comment: Tinted glass keeps its hue and gains alpha over the same blur. The
border takes the tint rather than the neutral hairline - at 35-70%,
which is why `border_alpha` is separate from `alpha`.

warn.use: the clearance callout, the active plan card

ref.use: the pipeline banner, anything about a reference body

active.use: a pill or segment in its selected state

$comment: AMBIENT LIGHT BEHIND THE GLASS, and it is not decoration: a blur with
nothing behind it to pick up renders as flat grey, and every panel in
the design then reads as the same slab. Both viewport containers carry
these two washes.
Percentages, so one string serves any size. Colours are phosphor and
pen-ref at low alpha - no new hues enter the palette here.
Non-visual constants the brief pins, kept here so neither client
invents one. `tap` is brief 6.3's one-handed requirement; `min_width`
is brief 6.7's quality floor.
